predecessors.name: Federal Republic of Central America
predecessors.text: the State of Honduras within the Federal Republic of Central America

ledger.x: 1838: Honduras leaves the Federal Republic of Central America.
1846: the eastern Mosquitia leaves the Honduran outline.
1859: Britain returns the northern Mosquito Coast.
1869: the northern bank of the Coco River is disputed.
1880: the capital moves from Comayagua to Tegucigalpa.
1960: the court settles the northern bank.
1960: Honduras receives the northern Mosquito Coast.
1971: the Swan Islands pass to Honduras.

wars.name: Guatemalan invasion of Honduras of 1906
wars.outcome: Honduras 'resisted an invasion from Guatemala in 1906' under President Manuel Bonilla; the page records no change of border.

wars.name: Football War
wars.outcome: No change of border on the page: 'In 1969, Honduras and El Salvador fought what became known as the Football War', and 'on 14 July 1969, the Salvadoran army invaded Honduras'.

certainty.note: The northern bank of the Coco River was disputed with Nicaragua from 1869 and the Mosquito Coast was under a British protectorate in 1844-1859; no page opened describes the frontiers with Guatemala or El Salvador.
The Nicaraguan frontier is the 1906 award confirmed by the ICJ in 1960 (terminal point 14 59.8 N, 83 08.9 W).
